exposure: Intended mode of birth (intended VBAC and vaginal birth, intended VBAC and cesarean, intended ERCS, intention uncertain)
Intended mode of birth (VBAC vs. ERCS)
cohort: 90,439 women in New South Wales between 2000 and 2012 with a primary cesarean who had a subsequent birth at term (>=37 weeks)
finding: Following a prior primary cesarean, there was a higher risk of transfusion associated with attempting VBAC compared with ERCS.
mod_finding: Risk of transfusion was almost four times higher for women classified as intended VBAC than intended ERCS (adjusted risk ratio = 3.73, 95% confidence interval 2.90-4.78).
